title: Authorize shared AI requests
responsibility: Checks current Write membership and the exact project revision before handing a request to its connected executor.

inputs.name: HubAgentController.constructor.context
inputs.description: Supplies the collaboration API, projection service, actor, request, project ID, and optional executor retained by this controller. The controller uses these values to authorize and handle requests; when the executor is absent, handle returns executor-offline after authorization succeeds.

outputs.name: HubAgentController.handle
outputs.description: The resolved value is the HTTP response for the request, including executor output or an offline, method-denied, or origin-denied response. Authorization, input parsing, snapshot validation, or an awaited dependency rejection can prevent resolution.

errors.name: forbidden
errors.description: Authorization fails with forbidden when the current project role is neither owner nor writer. If an executor is present, revocation is awaited first and its rejection can propagate instead.

errors.name: invalid-input
errors.description: The controller rejects with invalid-input for an unsupported method; an input that is not an object or names a different project; an event cursor without a string run ID and non-negative safe-integer after value; a startRun request ID that is not an 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal string; or missing or non-string revision branch or commit.

errors.name: revision-mismatch
errors.description: Projection validation rejects with revision-mismatch when the snapshot is not at the tip, its commit differs from the requested commit, or the requested branch is harness-evidence. This check runs for parsed methods other than providers and cancelRun, and does not run for the events cursor path.

errors.name: propagated rejection
errors.description: An awaited dependency rejection can reject handle, including from project lookup, revocation, executor availability or execution, body parsing, IPC validation, and projection snapshot lookup. A project lookup rejection is rethrown after optional revocation completes; if revocation rejects, that rejection propagates instead.
